headline: Octopuses have three hearts — ==and two of them stop== when they swim.

slides.label: The weird part
slides.heading: The main heart shuts off mid-swim — so octopuses prefer to crawl.
slides.body: Two hearts pump blood to the gills. The third serves the body — and it pauses under the strain of swimming. Crawling simply costs less energy.

slides.label: One more thing
slides.heading: Their blood is blue — copper does the job iron does in ours.
slides.body: Octopus blood uses haemocyanin, a copper-based molecule, to carry oxygen in cold, low-oxygen water. Copper makes it blue.

caption:
Three hearts. Blue blood. And they'd still rather walk.

headline: Archaeologists found ==3,000-year-old honey== in Egyptian tombs. Still edible.

slides.label: How
slides.heading: Honey is too dry and too acidic for bacteria to survive in.
slides.body: Bees fan the nectar until almost all its water is gone, and add an enzyme that makes it mildly antiseptic. Nothing that spoils food can live there.

slides.label: The catch
slides.heading: It only lasts forever ==if the jar stays sealed==.
slides.body: Let moisture in and honey can ferment like anything else. The tomb jars survived because they were shut tight for three millennia.

caption:
The only food in your kitchen with no expiry date.

headline: The Eiffel Tower gets ==15 cm taller== every summer.

slides.label: The physics
slides.heading: Iron expands in heat — 7,300 tonnes of it expands a lot.
slides.body: On hot days the metal swells and the tower grows up to 15 centimetres. In winter it shrinks right back.

slides.label: Bonus
slides.heading: The sun also makes it ==lean away== from itself.
slides.body: The side facing the sun expands more than the shaded side, tilting the top a few centimetres away from the sun as it moves.

caption:
Paris's most famous landmark has a summer growth spurt.

headline: Botanically, a banana is ==a berry== — and a strawberry isn't.

slides.label: The rule
slides.heading: A berry must grow from one flower with one ovary. Bananas qualify.
slides.body: So do grapes, tomatoes, kiwis and chillies. The 'berry' in strawberry is marketing, not botany.

slides.label: So what's a strawberry?
slides.heading: An 'accessory fruit' — the red part isn't even the fruit.
slides.body: The actual fruits are the tiny yellow seeds on the outside. The juicy red flesh is the swollen base of the flower.

caption:
Everything you knew about berries is wrong.
